newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian T-bills recover losses, prices seen down.
newsitem.headline: Russian T-bills recover losses, prices seen down.

text.p: Treasury bill prices rose on Thursday by up to 0.4 percentage points as investors bought shorter-dated paper to profit from higher yields emerging after a sell-off at the start of the week, dealers said.

But they said prices could ease on Friday as turnover relative to funds deposited in the system was low on Thursday, pointing to weak underlying demand. But some of Thursday's four trillion roubles deposited in the system were probably left over from Wednesday's extra bond trading session, they added.
The rouble firmed during the day on predominantly speculative trading.
* Average yield fell to 18.1 from 18.9 pct on Tuesday
* Turnover fell to 5.11 trillion roubles from 5.32 trillion
* Dealers deposited 3.95 trillion roubles in system before trading against 820.9 billion on Tuesday
* Central bank sold $429.98 billion of bills and bonds for
the Finance Ministry, raising $410.61 billion

Mikhail Vasilyev, deputy head of the securities
department at Aljba-Alliance said a flattening yield curve at the beginning of the week had pushed investors into less risky shorter-term issues.
"So issues maturing in October to February enjoyed most interest today," he said.
Prices fell earlier in the week because a shortage of roubles, as operators sought funds for Wednesday's government securities auctions, caused investors to liquidate some positions.
--Anna Smirnova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
